subject: general
question: Which of the following is a compound?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Water (H₂O)** is a compound because it is formed by the chemical combination of two elements, hydrogen and oxygen, in a fixed ratio of 2:1.
 
• It has distinct chemical properties different from the properties of its constituent elements (hydrogen and oxygen).
 
• Water is a pure substance that cannot be separated into its elements by physical means but can be broken down into hydrogen and oxygen through electrolysis.
 
• It is essential for life on Earth, forming a major part of biological systems and being involved in various physical and chemical processes.
 
• As a compound, water exhibits unique properties like high boiling and melting points, surface tension, and its ability to dissolve numerous substances, making it a universal solvent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxygen (O₂):**

 
 
• Oxygen is an element and exists as a diatomic molecule (O₂) in its most stable form.
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas essential for respiration in living organisms and combustion reactions.
 
• Oxygen forms compounds with nearly all other elements and is a major component of the Earth's atmosphere (approximately 21%).
 
 
 
• **Iron (Fe):**
 
 
• Iron is a metallic element and is one of the most abundant elements on Earth.
 
• It is widely used in construction, manufacturing, and making alloys like steel.
 
• Iron is also essential for biological processes, as it is a key component of hemoglobin in blood, which transports oxygen throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur (S):**
 
 
• Sulphur is a non-metallic element commonly found in nature in its elemental form or as part of various compounds like sulfates and sulfides.
 
• It has diverse applications, including the production of sulfuric acid, fertilizers, and rubber vulcanization.
 
• Sulphur is essential for life as it forms part of amino acids like cysteine and methionine.
 
 
 
• **Compounds:**
 
 
• Compounds are substances formed when two or more elements chemically combine in a fixed proportion.
 
• They have properties distinct from their constituent elements.
 
• Examples include water (H₂O), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and sodium chloride (NaCl).
